stories.new_fact: AP reported an ICE officer shot and wounded 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garces Perez during a Sunday Austin traffic stop, and Austin's mayor called for an independent investigation.
stories.new_takeaway: The governance issue is not only the shooting; it is whether federal immigration enforcement leaves local institutions with a reliable evidence and accountability path after force is used.
stories.why_now: The shooting occurred Sunday, September 20, and was in the September 21 news cycle.
stories.previous_coverage: No prior seven-episode coverage of this incident or Austin ICE force transparency.
stories.uncertainty: ICE's account and the attorney's account conflict on removal-status context; investigative agency, footage access and local police role remain unresolved.
stories.watch: Body-camera or vehicle footage, a named outside investigative agency, and Austin police access to evidence.

stories.new_fact: Grove City has a September 21 City Council meeting while Issue 28, the Community Consent Amendment, is active for the November 3 ballot.
stories.new_takeaway: The local question is whether residents want a broad ballot-level development gate or a narrower response to data-center power, water and land-use concerns.
stories.why_now: Council meets tonight and voter education around the November 3 measure is current.
stories.previous_coverage: The tracker retired earlier Grove City data-center charter coverage until the September 28 vote or amended language; today's segment uses the current Issue 28 thresholds and council context.
stories.uncertainty: Whether voters understand the amendment as data-center-specific or a broader rule for schools, hospitals, parks, churches and employers is uncertain.
stories.watch: Council discussion, resident materials, legal interpretation and whether language is narrowed before the campaign intensifies.

stories.new_fact: Freddie Mac's UAD page says the November 2 UAD 3.6 mandate is quickly approaching and UAD 2.6 reports submitted on or after that date will receive a fatal UCDP message.
stories.new_takeaway: The affected workflow is appraisal ordering, data validation, collateral review and investor delivery for GSE-bound loans, especially files ordered before November but submitted after the deadline.
stories.why_now: The deadline is close enough to affect current September and October pipelines, even though the mandate was announced earlier.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent lending segments covered MGIC loan limits, Fannie MI outreach, VantageScore and rate/refi dynamics; none covered UAD 3.6 cutover operations.
stories.uncertainty: Actual lender readiness, appraiser software adoption and cutover policies for in-flight orders remain to be seen.
stories.watch: Lender and AMC instructions for assignments ordered before November but submitted after November 2.
stories.date_exception: Specialist-beat operational update with a current effective-date consequence; background announcement predates the episode but matters now for active pipelines.

stories.new_fact: Societe Generale's 2029 plan and related reporting put AI into a multi-year cost program, including an Anthropic partnership and a roughly 500 to 600 million euro savings target.
stories.new_takeaway: A large bank embedding AI in a cost target needs attribution controls that distinguish real workflow savings from restructuring, vendor renegotiation and ordinary technology modernization.
stories.why_now: The Capital Markets Day plan and reporting were dated September 21.
stories.previous_coverage: Prior AI in Banking segments covered Ant, Mastercard, Schwab, Zopa, Goldman and Truist; none used a bank strategy-day cost-attribution target.
stories.uncertainty: No audited workflow metric, software-quality baseline, release-cycle measure or isolated AI savings result was disclosed.
stories.watch: Future SocGen disclosures separating AI-enabled savings from broader operating-cost reductions.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Added Societe Generale / AI-supported IT operations and internal productivity cost program as announced target; evidence rank reputable reporting plus company strategy materials; no measured workflow baseline disclosed.

stories.new_fact: AP reported Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. proposed a notification mechanism with China for AI incidents affecting national security.
stories.new_takeaway: The frontier governance thread moved from private lab restraint and export controls toward a possible government-to-government incident channel.
stories.why_now: Bessent described the proposal after Sunday talks in New York and ahead of this week's Trump-Xi White House meeting.
stories.previous_coverage: September 20 covered the AI slowdown antitrust lawsuit; this is a different mechanism, focused on state-level incident notification.
stories.uncertainty: There is no signed mechanism yet, no published scope, and no disclosed obligation for labs or cloud providers.
stories.watch: Written U.S.-China mechanism, joint statement, incident scope, or confirmation that talks ended without a binding channel.
stories.frontier_bar: Policy that binds labs directly; government-to-government AI incident reporting and national-security transparency.

stories.new_fact: Early ETF quotes showed QQQ higher while SPY, TLT and USO were lower; AP reported Asian stocks rose after Bessent described U.S.-China talks as successful and oil fell more than 2 percent as Hormuz traffic resumed.
stories.new_takeaway: Markets can price diplomatic relief and AI-linked growth while long rates still keep pressure on borrowers and lenders.
stories.why_now: The market data and AP market report were current for the Monday episode.
stories.previous_coverage: September 20 used compact ETF context; today's market item remains compact and updates the China-talk/oil backdrop.
stories.uncertainty: ETF pages are dynamic and premarket direction can change quickly.
stories.watch: Whether long-rate pressure eases enough to broaden relief beyond growth stocks.

stories.new_fact: Columbus forecast called for periods of rain Monday with a high near 64 and continued cool, cloudy, showery weather Tuesday and Wednesday.
stories.new_takeaway: The practical implication is slower commuting, indoor backups and wet field/job-site planning through midweek.
stories.why_now: Weather affects today's Columbus commute and planning.
stories.previous_coverage: Routine daily weather, not a repeated full story.
stories.uncertainty: Exact shower timing can change during the day.
stories.watch: Rain timing for morning and evening commutes.
